patients.summary: Retired construction foreman with long-standing poorly controlled insulin-treated type 2 diabetes, CKD 3a, hypertension and left knee osteoarthritis who joins the practice in 2023. In 2026 he has MSSA septic arthritis of the left knee treated with washout and antibiotics, then six months later MSSA lumbar vertebral osteomyelitis on home IV cefazolin at today.

Fax in today from Mr. Allard's former primary care office, 38 pages, scanned to Media. Notes run from 2020 through his last visit there in June 2023.

Abstracted for PCP before the 9/12 new patient visit:

- Med list (last updated 06/2023): Lantus 30 units nightly, Humalog per sliding scale with meals, lisinopril 10 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, Tylenol 500 mg every 6 hours as needed.
- Allergies: none recorded.
- Colonoscopy 2019 by outside GI: normal, no polyps, repeat in 10 years.
- Former smoker per their social history.
- No surgical history listed.
Original documents dated 2020-2023.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
62 y/o man transferring care. Retired construction foreman. Outside records reviewed before today (abstract in chart).

He has had type 2 diabetes for a long time and has been on insulin for years. Takes glargine 30 units at bedtime and lispro before meals off the sliding scale his last office gave him. Checks sugars most mornings, says fasting numbers run high, often 170s to 200s. No lows he knows of. Admits he eats late and does not always dose lispro before dinner. Was told his kidneys are 'stage 3' and his old doctor kept him on lisinopril for that and the pressure. Left knee has bothered him for years from the job, worse on stairs and after a long day on his feet; Tylenol takes the edge off. No chest pain, no dyspnea, no claudication, no numbness in his feet, no vision change.

PMH: T2DM on insulin, CKD 3a, HTN, L knee OA.
PSH: none.
Meds: glargine 30 u qhs, lispro SSI AC, lisinopril 10 daily, atorvastatin 40 daily, acetaminophen 500 q6h prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father had type 2 diabetes. Mother had osteoarthritis. Brother has chronic kidney disease.
SH: smoked for years, about 30 pack-years, quit in 2018. Drinks occasionally, one or two a week. No other substances. Retired.

Exam: well-appearing. BP a bit above where I want it for him but acceptable today. HEENT unremarkable. No thyromegaly. Heart regular rate and rhythm without murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen benign. Left knee with bony enlargement and medial joint line tenderness, crepitus, no effusion, no warmth, full extension, flexion a little limited. Feet: skin intact, no calluses or ulcers, monofilament intact bilaterally, DP pulses 2+.

A/P
1. T2DM, poorly controlled by his own logs. A1c, CMP, UACR today. Went over timing of lispro with meals and the late dinners. Keep glargine 30 for now and see where the A1c lands.
2. CKD 3a: creatinine/eGFR and UACR today. Continue ACE inhibitor. Avoid NSAIDs; he says he mostly sticks to Tylenol.
3. HTN: continue lisinopril 10.
4. Lipids: on atorvastatin 40 with his diabetes; lipid panel, continue.
5. L knee OA: acetaminophen as needed, stay active.
6. Health maintenance: PCV20 and flu shot today. Hep C and HIV screens with labs. Colonoscopy 2019 normal, next 2029. Meets criteria for lung cancer screening (30 pack-years, quit 2018): low-dose CT ordered. Optometry for a diabetic eye exam this year; he will call his usual eye office.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Your Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Mr. Allard, your results from Tuesday are back. Your A1c is above 9, which fits the high morning sugars you described, so diabetes is the main thing for us to work on. Kidney function is in the stage 3a range, as your old office had it, and potassium is fine. Urine protein is normal, which is good news. Cholesterol is well controlled on atorvastatin. Blood counts are normal. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were both negative.

Please try to take the lispro before each meal, including dinner, and send me your morning readings in a month. We will go over everything at your December visit.

reports.study: Low-dose CT chest for lung cancer screening
reports.text:
INDICATION: Annual lung cancer screening. 62-year-old former smoker, 30 pack-years, quit 2018. Baseline exam.
TECHNIQUE: Low-dose helical CT of the chest without IV contrast.
COMPARISON: None.
FINDINGS: Lungs: No pulmonary nodules. No consolidation or effusion. Airways patent. Mediastinum: No adenopathy. Heart size normal. Upper abdomen: Unremarkable. Bones: No aggressive osseous lesion.
reports.conclusion: Lung-RADS 1, negative. Continue annual screening with low-dose CT in 12 months.

documents.title: LDCT Result
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Screening CT negative, Lung-RADS 1. Portal message sent. Repeat next October.

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for 3 month check. Brought his meter. Morning readings mostly 160-210, a couple in the 140s. Says he has been better about lispro at dinner 'about half the time.' Weekends are the hardest. Knee unchanged, Tylenol once or twice a day on bad days. No hypoglycemia. Taking everything else as listed.

O: Vitals reviewed. Comfortable. Heart RRR, lungs clear. No edema. Feet without lesions.

Point-of-care draw today; A1c back while he was here, still above 9.

A/P:
- T2DM, poorly controlled. Discussed that his numbers are not where they need to be. He would like another few months working on meal timing and portion size before we change anything. Reasonable; continue glargine 30 u qhs and lispro sliding scale. Dietitian handout given.
- CKD 3a: creatinine stable compared with September.
- HTN: continue lisinopril.
- Knee OA: stable.
Recheck in 3 months with A1c and BMP.

documents.title: Refill Request
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Pharmacy fax requesting new Rx for insulin glargine pens and insulin lispro pens; old prescriptions written by previous PCP are out of refills. Pen needles also. Sent to PCP queue.

PCP: approved, 90-day supply with 3 refills each, sent electronically.

documents.title: Chronic Care Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Diabetes, CKD, BP recheck.

Doing a bit better with dinner doses since January. Fasting numbers more often in the 150s now. Still has some higher days. No lows. Knee about the same; he walks most days when the weather allows.

Exam: NAD. RRR. Clear lungs. No edema.

A1c improved some but still not at goal. Creatinine stable, K normal.

Plan:
- DM: some progress. Same glargine and lispro. Keep logging.
- CKD 3a, HTN: unchanged, continue lisinopril 10.
- Shingrix #1 today. Nurse visit in 2-3 months for the second dose.
RTC 6 months for physical.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Here for second Shingrix; missed the 6/11 slot, said he forgot. First dose 3/19, had a sore arm and felt tired for a day. No fever today, no new allergies. Shingrix 0.5 mL IM right deltoid, lot recorded. Waited 15 min, fine. Series complete.

documents.title: Knee
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi doc. Left knee has been barking more with this humid weather. Tylenol helps some. Is it ok to take it 4 times a day for a while or is that bad for my kidneys? Stan

documents.title: RE: Knee
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Stan, yes, acetaminophen up to 500 mg four times a day is fine for your kidneys and is the safer choice for you than ibuprofen or naproxen, which I'd avoid. If the knee swells up, gets hot, or you can't put weight on it, call us. Otherwise we'll look at it at your physical in September.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual exam, 63 y/o M.

Interval: no ER visits or hospital stays. Diabetes control slipped over the summer, he says, cookouts and a lot of ice cream. Fasting sugars back up near 200 some mornings. Knee about the same as always, Tylenol a few times a week. Eye exam in May, no retinopathy (report in chart). Mood good. Sleeping fine.

ROS: negative for chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, GI or GU complaints, foot numbness.

Meds unchanged: glargine 30 u qhs, lispro SSI with meals, lisinopril 10, atorvastatin 40, acetaminophen prn. NKDA.

Exam: Pleasant, in no distress. HEENT normal, TMs clear. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no masses. No edema. Left knee: bony hypertrophy and crepitus, no effusion. Feet: monofilament intact both feet, pulses good, skin intact. Skin: no concerning lesions.

Assessment/plan
- Preventive: Tdap and flu today. Shingrix complete. PCV20 done 2023. RSV vaccine is recommended for him with diabetes and kidney disease; he'll get it with his COVID shot at the pharmacy. Colonoscopy due 2029. Annual LDCT ordered for October.
- T2DM, uncontrolled: A1c pending today. Back to basics on dinner lispro and portions. Continue doses.
- CKD 3a: CMP and UACR today.
- HTN: continue lisinopril 10.
- Lipids: on atorvastatin 40, panel today.
- L knee OA: stable.
F/u December.

documents.title: Physical Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Stan, labs from your physical: A1c went back up, above 9 again, matching what you said about the summer. Kidney numbers steady at the same stage 3a level, potassium normal, liver tests normal. Cholesterol still good. Urine protein normal. Blood count normal. Let's keep at the dinner insulin and talk again in December.

documents.title: RE: Physical Results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks. Yeah I figured. I'll do better. See you in December.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
DM f/u. Holidays coming, he knows. Sugars about the same as September per meter, 170-220 fasting. Not missing glargine. Lispro still hit or miss at dinner. LDCT in Oct negative. RSV and COVID shots done at pharmacy.
Exam: RRR, lungs clear, no edema.
A1c today about the same as fall, still over 9.
A/P: T2DM uncontrolled, regimen unchanged for now; set a goal of lispro with every dinner and a 10-minute walk after. HTN and CKD stable, continue lisinopril. Return March with BMP and A1c beforehand.
